statement: Several producers push distinct values and several consumers pop concurrently; push/pop MAY fail spuriously under contention, but every SUCCESSFUL operation can be explained by ONE sequential FIFO executed in some order that respects each thread's own order; afterwards the queue holds exactly the values not yet popped, in FIFO order; no data race. Run alone afterwards, the queue holds exactly CAP items, fails (and returns) on full/empty, and stays FIFO across wrap-around.
contract: template<unsigned CAP> struct Queue { bool push(int v); bool pop(int& out); };  non-blocking: return false instead of waiting. CAP >= 2.
scenario_rule: every scenario has >= 2 producers or >= 2 consumers; total pushes exceed CAP in at least one scenario per capacity; capacities include a non-power-of-two (3), because modulo 2 hides index-direction bugs (found by `rashomon mutate`)
consistency: sequential consistency of the object w.r.t. per-thread order (plus join happens-before for the drain); weaker than real-time linearizability, which has no clean definition under weak memory without imposing extra synchronization
liveness_note: GenMC's spin-loop liveness heuristic misreports lock-free retry loops (e.g. Vyukov) as livelocks, so this spec checks termination instead: every execution must be able to complete, and the solo phase forces the full/empty failure paths to return.
note: This is the contract Vyukov's bounded MPMC queue actually meets: a producer that has claimed a slot but not yet published it makes others see 'full'/'empty'.
